sections.content:
You know *tan* … *como* from A2 Unit 6 ("as … as") and *de modo que* from the last lesson. If you put *que* after *tan* instead of *como*, you do not compare two things any more: you measure how much of something led to a result.

• *tan* + adjective or adverb + *que*: *Estaba tan cansado que se durmió en el sofá.* ("He was so tired that he fell asleep on the sofa.")
• *tanto*, *tanta*, *tantos*, *tantas* + noun + *que*: it agrees with the noun. *Había tanta gente que no pudimos entrar.*
• verb + *tanto que*: *Llovió tanto que se inundó la calle.*
• *de tal manera que* and *de tal modo que*: "in such a way that". They look at the way something was done, and at what that way led to: *Organizó la reunión de tal manera que todos pudieron hablar.*

In all of these the result is real, so the verb after *que* is in the indicative.

items.spanish: Habla tan rápido que no lo entiendo.
items.english: He speaks so fast that I do not understand him.

items.spanish: Tenía tantos problemas que no sabía por dónde empezar.
items.english: I had so many problems that I did not know where to start.

items.spanish: Trabaja tanto que casi no duerme.
items.english: He works so much that he hardly sleeps.

items.spanish: Explicó el plan de tal modo que nadie tuvo dudas.
items.english: He explained the plan in such a way that nobody had doubts.

sections.content: *Tan* goes only before an adjective or an adverb, and it never changes. Before a noun use *tanto* and make it agree: *tantos problemas*, never *tan problemas*. After a verb use *tanto*: *Llovió tanto que…*.
